results.instruction: Introduce the project and materials for making a floating display shelf.
Show the reclaimed pine boards that will be used for the shelf.
Cut the boards to size using a table saw.
Rip the boards to the desired width on the table saw.
Measure and mark the length for each board after cutting them square.
Cut grooves across the boards approximately 5 inches from each end.
Cut a groove in the wood to accommodate a three-quarter inch dowel bracket.
Cut another lengthwise groove to accommodate the base.
Cut the second groove lengthwise along the wood.
Sandwich the boards together to form the shelf structure.
Adjust the table saw blade height and position.
Place a sacrificial fence on the table saw.
Verify that the boards have a 3/4 inch hole for the dowel after sanding.
Raise the dado stack on the table saw to about half an inch.
Run both boards through the table saw to make a pocket for the base of the bracket.
Apply wood glue to the edges of the wooden pieces.
Nail the pieces together using three bread nails.
Allow the glue to dry.
Remove the clamps from the assembled bracket.
Cut the wooden bracket to size using a table saw.
Apply glue to the wooden bracket using a brush.
Insert dowels into the pre-drilled holes on the wooden bracket.
Mark the position of the holes on the wooden dowel using a pencil.
Cut the wooden dowel to size using a table saw.
Drill holes into the wooden dowel using a drill press.
Cut the wooden dowel to the desired length using a table saw.
Apply glue to the wooden dowel using a brush.
Apply glue to the dowel hole.
Spread the glue evenly inside the hole using a small brush.
Insert the dowel into the glued hole.
Tap the dowel flush with the surface using a mallet.
Repeat the gluing and insertion process for the second dowel.
Cut the remaining stock to strips about a quarter inch thick using a table saw.
Apply glue to the edge of the wooden piece.
Attach the cut strip to the glued edge.
Use a clamp to secure the wooden strip to the board.
Apply wood glue to the edge of another wooden board using a small brush.
Press the long wooden strip onto the glued edge of the board.
Use a clamp to secure the wooden strip to the board.
Measure and mark the wooden strip with a pencil.
Cut the marked wooden strip with a utility knife.
Apply wood glue to the cut wooden strip using a small brush.
Press the glued wooden strip onto the edge of the board.
Use a clamp to secure the wooden strip to the board.
Sand the edges of the wooden board with sandpaper.
Sand the top surface of the wooden board with sandpaper.
Use a heat gun to dry the sanded wooden board.
Inspect the dried wooden board for smoothness.
Apply a coat of varnish to the wooden board using a paintbrush.
Allow the varnish to dry on the wooden board.
Place a yellow electronic stud finder against the wall and use a pencil to mark the center of the detected stud where the red light indicates.
Position a metal L-bracket over the pencil mark on the wall and use a power drill to drive screws into the wall to secure the bracket.
Slide the painted wooden shelf onto the mounted metal bracket.
Use a power drill to drive small screws through the bracket into the underside of the shelf to secure it in place.
Place a black CD player on top of the installed white shelf.
